name: Medicare Care Compare
description: Compare published Medicare provider and quality information.
next_step: Compare published Medicare provider and quality information.

name: Pension additions: Aid and Attendance or Housebound
description: Extra monthly payments added to VA pension for qualifying veterans or survivors who need daily help or are housebound.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative about pension eligibility and Aid and Attendance. For a nursing home resident, ask about VA Form 21-0779; medical evidence is also required.

name: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation
description: A potential survivor benefit when a service member died in the line of duty or a veteran’s death meets VA’s service-related or other qualifying rules.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative whether DIC should be explored and what evidence is needed.

name: Increased VA disability compensation
description: A review route for an existing service-connected disability that has worsened.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative what evidence may support a request for an increased rating.

name: VA Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers
description: A VA caregiver assistance program with specific veteran and caregiver eligibility requirements.
next_step: Ask the VA caregiver support team about eligibility and the application process.

name: VA Program of General Caregiver Support Services
description: VA resources and support for people caring for veterans.
next_step: Ask the veteran’s VA care team which caregiver supports fit the situation.

name: VA hospice care
description: VA hospice care focuses on comfort and support near the end of life.
next_step: Ask the treating clinician or VA social worker about hospice assessment and coordination.

name: VA palliative care
description: Palliative care addresses symptoms, comfort and care goals for serious illness.
next_step: Ask the treating clinician about palliative care options.

name: VA pension during Medicaid-covered nursing home care
description: VA pension payments can be affected by Medicaid-covered nursing home care. The rules depend on the beneficiary’s circumstances.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative and the care facility’s benefits staff to review VA pension and Medicaid together before changing benefits.

name: Survivors Pension
description: A potential monthly benefit for qualifying surviving spouses and dependent children of wartime veterans, subject to income, net worth and other requirements.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative to screen for Survivors Pension and explain the evidence needed.

name: VA burial allowance and memorial routes
description: Ask the county office or VA burial program about the correct application.
next_step: Ask the county office or VA burial program about the correct application.

name: VA Community Living Centers
description: VA-operated Community Living Centers provide nursing home level care for eligible veterans.
next_step: Ask the VA care team or social worker about eligibility, assessment and local availability.

name: VA Community Nursing Home program
description: A VA pathway for care in participating community nursing homes, subject to eligibility and available services.
next_step: Ask the resident’s VA care team or social worker about community nursing home options.

name: VA health care enrollment
description: Apply for VA health care or get help understanding the enrollment process.
next_step: Call VA enrollment or ask your county veterans office about the application and supporting information.

public_contact.phone_label: VA health care enrollment line

name: Veterans Pension
description: Monthly pension for qualifying wartime veterans who meet age or disability, income, net worth and service requirements.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative to screen for pension and explain how care expenses may affect the application.

name: We Honor Veterans public resources
description: Use public veteran-care resources and ask the clinical team about coordinated care.
next_step: Use public veteran-care resources and ask the clinical team about coordinated care.
organization: National Alliance for Care at Home

name: VA Home Improvements and Structural Alterations (HISA)
description: Medically necessary changes to a veteran’s primary home, including permanent ramps, accessible bathrooms and widened access. Some non-service-connected needs can qualify.
next_step: Ask your VA care team for a clinical review and contact your VA medical facility’s Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service. Confirm your remaining lifetime benefit and obtain the HISA application checklist.
constraints: HISA excludes portable ramps, stair glides, new construction and routine home repairs. VA determines eligibility, medical necessity and the available benefit. Prepare VA Form 10-0103, a VA-written or approved prescription, owner authorization (notarized for renters), an itemized estimate and a before photograph.

name: VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant
description: A housing grant route for veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities.
next_step: Review the qualifying disability and ownership rules with VA or an accredited representative. Apply online through VA or use VA Form 26-4555; ask VA about project planning and approval before construction.
constraints: These grants require specific qualifying service-connected disabilities; a disability rating alone does not establish eligibility. Confirm the current fiscal-year maximum and any benefit already used with VA.

name: VA Special Housing Adaptation (SHA) grant
description: A housing adaptation grant route with specific service-connected disability requirements.
next_step: Review the qualifying disability and ownership rules with VA or an accredited representative. Apply online through VA or use VA Form 26-4555; ask VA about project planning and approval before construction.
constraints: These grants require specific qualifying service-connected disabilities; a disability rating alone does not establish eligibility. Confirm the current fiscal-year maximum and any benefit already used with VA.

name: Get a missing DD214 or service record
description: Request military records that may help document service for a benefits application.
next_step: Use the National Archives request instructions or ask the county veterans office for help. Who may request records and any fee depend on the record and request.

name: Find accredited help with a VA claim
description: Find and appoint an accredited representative for a benefits claim or decision review. Accredited VSO claims assistance is free.
next_step: Use VA’s representative search, then ask the representative if they are available. Attorneys and claims agents may charge fees.

name: Find a VA medical facility or benefits office
description: Search for VA locations near the resident and identify where to ask about care or benefits.
next_step: Use the official locator with the resident’s city or ZIP code and select the kind of facility needed.

name: Veteran housing and homelessness help
description: A 24-hour VA contact for veterans who are homeless or at risk of losing housing.
next_step: Call 877-424-3838, available 24/7, if homeless or at risk of losing housing. Family, care teams and supporters may also call. Ask for local VA and community housing support.

name: VA Temporary Residence Adaptation (TRA)
description: Changes to a family member’s home where a qualifying veteran or service member is living temporarily.
next_step: Ask VA about TRA if you qualify for SAH or SHA and are temporarily living in a family member’s home.
constraints: TRA requires SAH or SHA eligibility; it is not a general temporary-housing or renter grant.

name: Memory loss and dementia: 24/7 support
description: Free, confidential dementia information, caregiver support and referrals to local community resources.
next_step: Call the Alzheimer’s Association helpline for care planning, local support groups and caregiver guidance. Seek medical evaluation for new memory concerns.
constraints: The helpline provides support and referrals; it does not replace clinical assessment or emergency services.

name: American Legion: find a local post
description: Official post lookup for community connections and identifying public contacts to share the guide with.
next_step: Search the official directory for your town or ZIP code. Confirm the post’s public phone or email and ask who handles community partnerships.
constraints: A local post is not automatically an accredited claims office or a funding provider. Confirm its services, membership or visitor rules, accessibility and current contact details.

name: Suicide and emotional crisis support: 988
description: Crisis counseling and referrals for people in suicidal crisis or emotional distress, including veterans and concerned supporters.
next_step: Call or text 988 for crisis support. Veterans-specific support is available through the call service. For immediate danger, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department.
constraints: Crisis support is separate from benefits eligibility and scheduled mental health treatment.

name: Veterans: mental health care and suicide prevention
description: VA mental health care, suicide-prevention guidance, counseling and routes to VA medical centers and Vet Centers. Some services are available without VA enrollment.
next_step: Use the VA page to connect with care. Existing patients can ask their primary care provider; others can contact a VA medical center or Vet Center. For urgent emotional distress, use 988 instead of waiting for an appointment.
constraints: Confirm which services fit the person’s eligibility and needs. Scheduled care is not a substitute for immediate crisis help.

name: Housing stability: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
description: Housing stability services through community organizations for low-income veteran families experiencing homelessness or imminent housing loss.
next_step: Use the SSVF Providers link on the VA page to find an awarded organization. Ask about county coverage, prevention or rapid rehousing, eligibility and current assistance.
constraints: Provider service areas, funding and eligibility vary. An award or referral does not guarantee financial assistance.

name: HUD-VASH: housing vouchers and VA support
description: Housing voucher assistance paired with VA case management for veterans experiencing homelessness who need ongoing support.
next_step: Call VA homelessness routing at 877-424-3838 and ask whether HUD-VASH screening is appropriate. Ask about local assessment, vouchers and housing availability.
constraints: Screening, program criteria, voucher availability and qualifying housing requirements apply; immediate housing is not guaranteed.
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs / HUD

name: VA Community Resource and Referral Centers
description: Find walk-in community resource centers connecting homeless and at-risk veterans with VA and non-VA services.
next_step: Use the official center directory and confirm the nearest location, hours and intake. If no nearby center is listed, call VA homelessness routing at 877-424-3838.
constraints: Centers are not present in every county. Confirm local access and resources; a listing does not guarantee a shelter bed.

name: Georgia veterans: accredited claims help
description: Free help with VA claims, applications and appeals for veterans and families.
next_step: Choose your county for its GDVS Veterans Field Service Office, or call the main line and ask which office serves your county. Appointments are preferred; many offices schedule online through ReFrame.
